children: China's travel spending remains a bright spot amid tepid consumer demand, according to BofA Securities in a research note. "More than half of the survey respondents took or booked more overnight trips than last summer," the bank says, citing its own survey. Travel demand was also led by higher-income households, pointing to an uneven recovery, BofA says. Higher airfares following the global energy shock prompted consumers to switch transport modes, choose closer destinations instead of abandoning the trips altogether, the bank says. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)
